summary: A proposed action held until a person approves, rejects or amends it. It renders the decision; it does not enforce it.
useWhen: an agent proposes something with consequences — spending, sending, deleting, deploying, changing permissions
a regulated or audited process needs demonstrable human oversight at a specific point
the proposal is worth showing in full, in context, before it runs

useInstead.when: the action is already happening and needs stopping
a person initiated the action themselves and only needs to confirm it
useInstead.why: confirming your own request is a dialog; reviewing something proposed for you is a decision

useInstead.when: you are reporting what happened rather than asking

low.use: reversible and cheap — a draft, a local edit. Neutral surface

medium.use: the default. Real but recoverable consequences

high.use: spending, sending externally, deleting, granting access. Warning surface, deliberately not error

pending.use: the default, and the only state with actions

approved.use: resolved — the actions are replaced by the record

expired.use: nobody answered. The common real outcome, and the reason a gate cannot sit pending for ever

title.note: required, and the region's accessible name. Name the action and its object — "Delete 14 projects", never "Confirm action"

children.note: the evidence: the plan, the diff, the tool call. This is what the person is deciding about

resolution.note: shown in place of the actions once resolved; defaults to the status

guarantees: neither button is focused on mount — autofocusing approve turns a decision into an Enter keypress on an unread page
the title is programmatically focusable, so the caller can move focus to the question rather than to an answer
reject precedes approve in the DOM, so a keyboard reaches the safe answer first
resolution is announced once through a polite live region
focus is never trapped: an approval a user was rushed through is not oversight
requires: not acting until `onApprove` fires — this component gates nothing on its own
a `title` that names the action and its object
notes: `risk` changes emphasis and nothing else. It does not add confirmation, does not disable anything, and must never be read as a policy the component enforces.

antiPatterns.dont: treating the gate as the enforcement point
antiPatterns.why: it renders a decision. If your code acts before `onApprove`, there is no gate — only a picture of one
the page is the evidence; hiding it to ask about it removes what the decision needs
Enter on an unread page is not oversight, and it is exactly what an audit will look for

antiPatterns.dont: an approve-only gate with no reject
antiPatterns.why: a decision with one answer is a notification wearing a button

antiPatterns.dont: `onEdit` when the proposal cannot actually be amended
antiPatterns.why: an edit button that discards the edit is worse than no edit button
a gate nobody answered is indistinguishable from one that is broken
